claims.text: Introducing a fine dispersion of refractory carbide particles will enhance the high-temperature mechanical performance of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The carbide dispersion will preserve the alloy's thermal and irradiation stability.
Composition adjustment and controlled heat treatment can form uniformly distributed, nanometer-scale carbide particles in the alloy.
HfC or ZrC would be suitable stable carbide particles for this intervention.
The intervention will produce nanometer-scale carbide precipitates both at grain boundaries and within grains.
Carbide particles will obstruct dislocation motion.
Carbide particles will obstruct grain-boundary sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase creep resistance.
Relative to the corresponding alloy without a carbide dispersion, the treated alloy will have higher yield strength at high temperature.
Relative to the corresponding alloy without a carbide dispersion, the treated alloy will have a slower high-temperature creep rate.
The treated alloy will maintain the same phase stability as the baseline under high irradiation flux.
The predicted improvement requires carbide particles to remain uniformly dispersed and finer than approximately 100 nm.
Carbide overgrowth, aggregation, or spatial inhomogeneity could eliminate the mechanical benefit or cause irradiation-associated brittleness.
